- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 5–10% in next 5–7d horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% downward bias to 30d forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 18d moving average if price deviates >±10%.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overreact to auction supply; dampen forecast by 2–5% per event beyond 15.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from bearish to bullish (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00), model often misreads momentum; delay upward adjustment by 1–2 days unless confirmed by 3 consecutive bullish sentiment.
- For 30d forecasts with low historical volatility, model tends to over-smooth; allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast range if sentiment is volatile or events are clustered.
